nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

H3 removes the usual task boundaries between generation modes. Text-to-video, image-to-video, first/last-frame control, and reference-driven generation (character, motion, camera, voice, style) are all handled by one model instead of separate expert pipelines.

## About this workflow

This template runs the **Image to Video** task (`MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo` node), which covers both:

- **t2va** (text-to-video), when no images are connected
- **fl2va** (first/last-frame image-to-video), when `first_frame` and/or `last_frame` are connected

**Key inputs**

- **first_frame / last_frame**: optional keyframes; the model generates the motion between them
- **prompt**: describe the shots, motion, and the accompanying audio (dialogue, SFX, music) in one block
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector. H3's native canvas is a 768px short edge, capped at 768x1344 pixels, rounded to a multiple of 32
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node, snapping up to the model's 17-frame-per-block (17k+5) grid at 24fps

## Model Storage Location

```
📂 ComfyUI/
├── 📂 models/
│   ├── 📂 vae/
│   │      ├── minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors
│   │      └── minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
│   │      └── minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   └── 📂 text_encoders/
│            └── qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors
```

## Report Issue

Note: Please update ComfyUI first ([guide](https://docs.comfy.org/installation/update_comfyui)) and prepare required models. Desktop/Cloud updates follow stable releases, so some nightly-supported models may not be available yet.

- Cannot run / runtime errors: [ComfyUI/issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues)
- UI / frontend issues: [ComfyUI_frontend/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/issues)
- Workflow issues: [workflow_templates/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/issues)

How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 0.00-second mark of the target video; Picture 2 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 8.00-second mark of the target video.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, the overgrown private courtyard shown in <Picture 1> holds the exact framing, camera angle, and composition of the first frame: a leafy tree and a folded black metal umbrella stand on the left, dense wild bushes across the middle, a weathered black chair and a small green child's chair on a gray wood deck, weeds pushing through the stone pavers, a wood-paneled wall with a black-framed glass door on the right, a Haier AC unit and large reflecting windows on the upper gray building, and a wooden bench with a wire rack at the right edge. The camera holds a static shot as a compressed multi-week construction time-lapse plays in a single continuous take while the daylight in the glass-door reflection shifts from bright midday toward dusk. A crew of workers moves in and out across the frame: they cut back the wild bushes and pull weeds from the pavers, drag away the folded umbrella stand, the black chair, the child's chair, the cluttered bags, and the old bench with its wire rack. Workers spread fresh gravel between the stone pavers and lay new clean slabs, strip the old deck planks and install new dark wood decking on the platform and steps, then fit warm LED strips under each step. Steel workers raise and weld the canopy frame with bright sparks, bolt the glass panels into the overhead pergola, build the left planter box, add soil, and plant evergreens, ferns, purple foliage, and ornamental grasses behind a new wire mesh fence. On the right, workers set the concrete counter, build the wood cabinets, place the stainless grill, stack firewood in the bin, and stand up the tall black heater with its utensils. Workers re-stain the wood-paneled slats darker, mount the wall sconce and hanging light, then carry in and arrange the curved gray sectional sofa with its fur throw and the round wooden coffee table on its circular stone base. By the end the same locked composition as <Picture 1> has become the finished patio of <Picture 2>: clean dark decking with glowing step lights, the glass canopy overhead, the planted left planter, the fully built grill station, and the warm sconce lit against a dusk sky reflected in the glass door.

overall_soundscape: Wind and birdsong fill the open courtyard as shears snip the wild bushes and weeds tear free of the pavers. Drills, hammers, and the bright hiss of welding punctuate the work while lumber drags across gravel, glass panels slide into the canopy, concrete settles in the new counter, and a worker's shouted call echoes. The day's ambient hum gives way to evening quiet as the finished patio's lights click on.

non_diegetic_music: A steady percussive pulse at a moderate tempo with layered metallic hits and rising string swells builds through the construction, then resolves into a soft sustained pad of low strings and a single piano tone as the lights turn on.
